title: Palm Sugar Lime Shrimp Skewers
seoTitle: Palm Sugar Lime Shrimp Skewers | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Shrimp skewer night—honey sriracha glaze, fast char, no generic kabob repeat
subtitle: Kaffir lime glazed jumbo shrimp, Thai basil, and char for ten
description: Jumbo shrimp marinate briefly in lime and garlic, grill on skewers until pink and 140°F, and glaze with honey-sriracha in the final minute.

steps.title: Marinate shrimp briefly
steps.instruction: Toss shrimp with half the lime juice, garlic, fish sauce, and salt. Marinate 20–30 minutes refrigerated only. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build honey sriracha glaze
steps.instruction: Whisk honey, sriracha, and remaining lime juice until smooth. Reserve for basting. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Heat grill hot
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to high, 450°F. Oil grates. Have glaze and brush ready. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Skewer shrimp
steps.instruction: Thread 4–5 shrimp per skewer in a flat line for even contact. Pat dry before grilling. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for fish, 145°F for shrimp until opaque on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Grill shrimp
steps.instruction: Grill skewers 2 minutes per side until pink, lightly charred, and 135–140°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze finish
steps.instruction: Brush honey sriracha and grill 30 seconds per side until sticky. Move to cooler zone if sugar burns. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for fish, 145°F for shrimp until opaque on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 2 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 140°F
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 2 minutes. Transfer to hotel pans, cover loosely, hold at 140°F up to 12 minutes max. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Serve with herbs
steps.instruction: Scatter cilantro and green onions at the line. About 8 oz shrimp per firefighter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Never marinate shrimp over 30 minutes—lime turns them mushy.
Flat skewer layout beats stacked shrimp for even char.
140°F hold max—shrimp tighten up fast above that.
tonightSpread: Honey sriracha shrimp skewers with lime and cilantro.
Coconut rice or quick noodle salad on the side.
leftovers: Pull shrimp for Thai-style lettuce wraps.
Chop into fried rice with extra sriracha.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shrimp skewers cook in under 10 minutes—ideal when the tone might drop. They hold covered at 140°F briefly and taste best with fresh lime at service.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate shrimp 20–30 minutes max—acid toughens longer soaks. Grill high 450°F, 2 minutes per side. Hold covered at 140°F up to 12 minutes. Glaze at service if needed.
